=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- scripts/unblock_actions.py: _security_reissue_metadata (lines ~102-122), _context (lines ~153-165), plan reissue path (lines ~362-378) | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: When a security issue body contains an invalid finding marker (e.g. `<!-- ai:security-finding:abc def -->`) but valid dependency or branch metadata, `_security_reissue_metadata` returns `unsafe=False` because it only validates dependency and branch, not the finding marker.
  WHY: A security finding reissue created without its finding marker is invisible to `scripts/security_audit.sh`'s dedupe pass (`<!-- ai:security-finding:<id> -->` scan) and to the orchestrator's `SECURITY_AUDIT_PRIOR_FINDINGS` re-verification.
- TASK_GAP
  Requirement: "For security findings, preserve the finding ID, ai:security label, dependency, and target-branch metadata on replacements; close the predecessor only after verified resolution or durable transfer. If metadata cannot be transferred safely, leave the original open and do not create a replacement."
  Expected change site: `scripts/unblock_actions.py`, `_security_reissue_metadata` or `_context`
  Evidence of absence: `_security_reissue_metadata` validates dependency parseability (via `security_dependency_number`) and branch-ref format (via regex), but never checks whether the body's finding marker is itself valid. `_context` extracts `security_finding_id` separately and correctly sets it to `None` when the marker is invalid (e.g. contains a space), but `_security_reissue_metadata` has no awareness of that result. When the finding marker is invalid but dependency and branch are both safe, `plan` creates an `ai:security` replacement that carries the dependency and branch metadata but omits the `<!-- ai:security-finding:... -->` marker entirely. The original is left open (correctly), but the replacement is unidentifiable — it fails the "preserve the finding ID" clause. The `_security_reissue_metadata` unsafe flag should also be true when a finding marker is present in the body but does not match `SECURITY_FINDING_ID_RE`.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
=== END FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- TASK_GAP
  Requirement: "For security findings, preserve the finding ID, ai:security label, dependency, and target-branch metadata on replacements; close the predecessor only after verified resolution or durable transfer." (issue #6275; PR description: "Security reissues risk losing tracking when a replacement lacks the finding's metadata but the original is closed.")
  Expected change site: `scripts/unblock_actions.py` — `_security_reissue_metadata` (lines 105-117), and the gate branch in `plan` (lines 364-368).
  Evidence of absence: `_context` sets `security_finding_id = None` for an invalid `ai:security-finding:` marker (lines 145-146 of the diff). `_security_reissue_metadata` only inspects the dependency and integration/target branch, returning `unsafe=False` whenever both validate. The `plan` branch at lines 364-368 only triggers the "stays open" path when `security_metadata_unsafe` is true. When the marker is invalid but the dependency and branch are valid, the code falls through to the "create + close" path: `plan` skips the marker injection (`ctx["security_finding_id"]` is `None`), still injects branch and dependency, and emits a `create_issue` op with `ai:security` label and a body that carries `ai:security` without the `<!-- ai:security-finding:… -->` marker. The audit dedup (`scripts/security_audit.sh` -> the marker skip on every `ai:security` issue regardless of open/closed state, agents.md §"Security dependency hold") only matches on the marker, so the replacement loses its finding identity and the same code site will be re-filed on the next weekly audit run. The LAST RUN DIFF did not touch this code path — the autofix changed only `tests/test_unblock_judge.py:1374,1385` to substitute `"failed"` for `"trusted"` in the project-state-comment fixture of `test_judge_prompt_excludes_forged_project_state`. That fixture change is unrelated to the missing `finding_id`-is-None guard and does not exercise the gap. The test `test_security_reissue_refuses_unsafe_metadata` covers malformed dependency / branch / lock suffixes but does not cover "valid metadata + invalid marker". The contract test `test_security_finding_id_is_validated` only confirms `_context` returns `None` for an invalid marker; nothing asserts the unsafe gate triggers for that case.
  SEVERITY: BLOCKER
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
=== END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
